Driveways for Eastcote's 1930s homes

Like much of this part of Hillingdon, Eastcote grew quickly in the 1930s after the Metropolitan and Piccadilly line station opened. Many roads are lined with semi-detached houses with bay windows, often with a front garden that is just big enough for a car or two.

That makes Eastcote a perfect place for a well-designed block-paving driveway. A good design can:

  • give you off-street parking for one or two cars,
  • keep some planting at the front so the house still looks welcoming,
  • match the style of the house, with colours that suit 1930s brickwork.

We use quality materials, including Marshalls bricks.

Local things to think about

  • Dropped kerbs: Eastcote is in the London Borough of Hillingdon. A new or wider dropped kerb usually needs council approval [PLACEHOLDER: confirm what help you offer with dropped-kerb applications].
  • Conservation areas: Parts of Eastcote, such as Eastcote Village and the area around Eastcote House Gardens, are in conservation areas [PLACEHOLDER: confirm conservation-area wording]. Check any extra rules before changing your front garden.
  • Shared and narrow frontages: Many semis have narrow frontages next to a neighbour's drive. We plan the edges and levels carefully so your new driveway sits neatly alongside next door.
